title: Parallel Courses
summary: Given an integer n representing n courses labeled 1 to n, and an array relations indicating prerequisite relationships, determine the minimum number of semesters needed to complete all courses.
statement: Given an integer n representing n courses labeled 1 to n, and an array relations indicating prerequisite relationships, determine the minimum number of semesters needed to complete all courses. If it's impossible, return -1. Courses can be taken in any number in a semester, but all prerequisites must be met before taking a course.
constraints: Each relation [a,b] requires a before b.
Take unlimited ready courses per term; return minimum terms or -1 on a cycle.
reference_solution:
def minimum_course_terms(n, relations):
 adjacent=[[] for _ in range(n)];degree=[0]*n
 for x,y in relations:adjacent[x-1].append(y-1);degree[y-1]+=1
 current=[i for i,d in enumerate(degree) if d==0];terms=completed=0
 while current:
  terms+=1;following=[]
  for course in current:
   completed+=1
   for other in adjacent[course]:degree[other]-=1;following.append(other) if degree[other]==0 else None
  current=following
 return terms if completed==n else -1

hints: Each topological BFS layer is one semester of simultaneously ready courses.
Track indegrees and begin with all zero-indegree nodes.
Remove one layer, unlock its successors, and count layers; detect a cycle by incomplete count.
Dependencies force successive layers, while every course within a layer can run together.
